_readme: Copy this to /etc/belabox-hotplug/modem-apn.json and edit it for your SIMs.
Keys starting with an underscore are ignored by the loader (JSON has no comments).
RESOLUTION ORDER (match_order below):  iccid -> imsi_plmn -> carrier -> default
Your own per-ICCID entries deliberately outrank the shipped carrier table.
The table is keyed on the HOST network's PLMN, but an MVNO SIM broadcasts the
host's PLMN while needing a different APN - a Tello SIM reports 310260
(T-Mobile) yet needs 'wholesale', not 'fast.t-mobile.com'. If the table were
consulted first, every MVNO would match its host carrier's row and the
per-ICCID override would never be reached for exactly the SIMs it exists for.
Matching always uses the SIM's HOME PLMN (ModemManager's SIM operator-code, or
the IMSI split using the MNC length from the SIM's EF_AD), never the network
the modem is currently registered on - a roaming SIM would otherwise match
whichever local carrier it happened to camp on.
Find your SIM's ICCID / IMSI / home PLMN with:  python3 modem-apn-fix.py --list
_readme_carriers: !!! THIS TABLE GOES STALE. Carrier APNs change, networks get retired and MVNOs
get acquired. It is a good starting point, NOT a permanently authoritative
source. Spot-check it against each carrier's own current documentation
periodically, and re-check any entry the moment a SIM won't attach.
Bump _apn_table_reviewed when you do; the script warns once it is over a year old.
Entries WITHOUT mcc_mnc_prefixes cannot be matched automatically - MVNOs ride
their host carrier's PLMN, so there is nothing unique to match on. They are
reference data: point an ICCID prefix at one to use it, e.g.
apn_variant_order picks which field of a matched entry is used. 'apn_5g' is
deliberately NOT in the default order: an EM7455 is LTE-only Cat-6 hardware.
Note for standalone modems: AT&T documents 'Broadband' (apn_hotspot) for
tablets/hotspots/modem devices rather than NXTGENPHONE. A BELABOX modem is
arguably one of those, but it depends on the plan the SIM is on - so the
default order still prefers 'apn'. Override per-SIM with

AT&T.notes: Use NXTGENPHONE for LTE devices, ENHANCEDPHONE for 5G-capable devices, Broadband for tablets/standalone hotspot/modem devices specifically.

T-Mobile.notes: Same APN for LTE and 5G, data and MMS. Sprint's network was fully retired June 30, 2022 - all former Sprint IMSIs now route through T-Mobile and use this APN. UScellular was acquired by T-Mobile (completed Aug 1, 2025) and migrated lines also use this APN.

Verizon.notes: Single APN covers 4G, 5G, and MMS. Verizon SIMs also auto-provision background APNs (vzwims, vzwadmin) - do not touch or duplicate these, only vzwinternet needs explicit configuration if not auto-populated. Verizon retired 3G CDMA entirely on Dec 31, 2022.

Cricket Wireless (AT&T MVNO).notes: Newer Cricket SIMs may require 'endo' instead of 'ndo' - check both if one fails. No mcc_mnc_prefixes: Cricket rides AT&T's PLMNs, so it can only be selected via an explicit ICCID entry.

Consumer Cellular.notes: Dual-network MVNO - underlying network (AT&T vs T-Mobile) must be determined per-SIM, values are not interchangeable. Field names here are non-standard on purpose so nothing is picked automatically; select one with an explicit ICCID entry, e.g. {"carrier": "Consumer Cellular", "variant": "apn_att_network"}.

Boost Mobile (independent, EchoStar/DISH.notes: Boost is now its own network (no longer Sprint-based) as of the DISH divestiture; boost.data is current, Boost_Mobile is legacy fallback only.

_readme_maps: apn_by_iccid_prefix: keys are ICCID prefixes - use as many digits as you need.
A short prefix covers a whole carrier's SIM batch; a full 19-20 digit ICCID pins
one specific SIM and, being longer, overrides the short one.
apn_by_imsi_plmn: keys are the home PLMN (MCC+MNC). Use this to override a row
in the carrier table without editing the table itself.
